name: Home Medical Service
description: Doctors and nurses visit seniors at home to manage chronic conditions, do health assessments, and provide medical care for those who cannot travel to clinics.
eligibility: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 65 and above (or younger if medically indicated) who have difficulty travelling to clinics. Referral by a doctor or AIC required.
costGuide: Subsidised rates based on means testing. From $5 per visit for those on CHAS/Pioneer Generation. Full fee around $80–$120 per visit.
howToAccess: Call AIC at 1800-650-6060 or ask your doctor/hospital Medical Social Worker for a referral.

name: Home Nursing Service
description: Registered nurses visit at home to provide wound care, medication management, tube feeding, catheter care, and monitoring of health conditions.
eligibility: Seniors who are medically stable but need ongoing nursing care at home. Must be Singapore Citizen or PR. Referral by hospital or doctor needed.
costGuide: Subsidised from $5–$15 per visit with means testing. Unsubsidised around $60–$100 per visit.
howToAccess: Hospital discharge planner, Medical Social Worker, or AIC hotline at 1800-650-6060.

name: Home Personal Care Service
description: Trained care workers assist seniors at home with personal hygiene (bathing, grooming, toileting), mobility, and simple health monitoring.
eligibility: Frail seniors who need daily personal care support. Singapore Citizens and PRs. Income-based means testing applies.
costGuide: Subsidised from $3–$10 per session. Full rate around $20–$35 per session. Home Caregiving Grant may offset costs.
howToAccess: AIC hotline 1800-650-6060 or through a Senior Care Centre / day care referral.

name: Home Therapy Service
description: Physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and speech therapists visit at home to help seniors regain function, improve mobility, adapt to assistive devices, and train caregivers.
eligibility: Seniors who cannot travel to a rehab centre and require therapy. Referral from a doctor or hospital required. Citizens and PRs.
costGuide: Subsidised from $10–$30 per session. Full fee $80–$150 per session.
howToAccess: Hospital discharge team or AIC hotline 1800-650-6060.

name: Interim Caregiver Service
description: Short-term paid caregiver support for seniors recently discharged from hospital while family caregivers are arranging long-term care. Typically up to 3 months.
eligibility: Seniors recently discharged from hospital who need temporary caregiver support. Referral via hospital Medical Social Worker.
costGuide: Subsidised rates available. Approximately $20–$50 per day based on hours needed. AIC administers subsidy.
howToAccess: Ask the hospital's Medical Social Worker or discharge planner before leaving the hospital.

name: Meals on Wheels
description: Regular delivery of nutritious meals to homebound seniors who are unable to cook for themselves, supporting their nutrition and enabling regular wellness checks.
eligibility: Homebound seniors aged 60 and above who are unable to prepare their own meals. Singapore Citizens and PRs. Means testing applies.
costGuide: Subsidised from $2 per meal. Some providers offer free meals for very low-income seniors.
howToAccess: Through AIC, Care Corner, or nearest Senior Activity Centre. Call AIC at 1800-650-6060.
source: Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) / Care Corner

name: Senior Care Centre (SCC)
description: Day programme combining nursing care, therapy, and activities for frail seniors who need daytime supervision. Provides respite for family caregivers.
eligibility: Seniors who are not bedridden but need daytime care and supervision. Citizens and PRs. Means testing for subsidies.
costGuide: Subsidised from $6–$25 per day based on means testing. Full fee $50–$120 per day. Pioneer/Merdeka Generation receive additional subsidies.
howToAccess: AIC hotline 1800-650-6060 or Care Corner to find nearest SCC.

name: Day Rehabilitation Centre
description: Intensive rehabilitation at a centre for seniors recovering from stroke, falls, surgery, or other conditions. Includes physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy.
eligibility: Seniors recovering from acute medical episodes who need structured rehab but do not require inpatient care. Doctor referral required.
costGuide: Subsidised from $15–$50 per day. Full fee $80–$200 per day.
howToAccess: Hospital discharge planner or AIC hotline 1800-650-6060.

name: Dementia Day Care
description: Structured day programme specifically designed for seniors with dementia, providing cognitive stimulation, personal care, and caregiver respite in a safe environment.
eligibility: Seniors diagnosed with dementia. Citizens and PRs preferred. Referral from doctor or AIC.
costGuide: Subsidised from $8–$30 per day. Dementia-specific subsidies may apply through AIC.
howToAccess: AIC hotline 1800-650-6060 or Dementia Singapore (formerly Alzheimer's Disease Association) at 6377 0700.
source: Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) / Dementia Singapore

name: Active Ageing Centre (AAC)
description: Community hub offering social activities, health screenings, fitness classes, and light support for relatively independent seniors. Promotes active ageing and prevents social isolation.
eligibility: Seniors aged 60 and above who are relatively independent. No means testing required for most programmes.
costGuide: Most programmes are free or low-cost ($2–$10). Managed by community partners under IMDA/MOH.
howToAccess: Find the nearest AAC through AIC's website or call 1800-650-6060.

name: Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)
description: Monthly cash grant of up to $400 for families caring for a senior with moderate to severe disability at home. Reduces financial burden of caregiving.
eligibility: Senior must be a Singapore Citizen with moderate to severe disability (score of 2 or less on the Functional Assessment for Rehabilitation), living at home (not in nursing home). Household per capita income must not exceed $3,200/month.
howToAccess: Apply online via AIC's website or in person at any AIC APCC (Agency for Integrated Care office). Documents needed: NRIC, income documents, bank account details.

name: Caregivers Training Grant (CTG)
description: Annual training subsidy of up to $200 per year for caregivers to attend approved courses on caregiving skills, reducing risk of caregiver burnout and improving quality of care.
eligibility: Caregivers of seniors/persons with disabilities. Caregiver must be a Singapore Citizen or PR. The care recipient must be a Singapore Citizen.
costGuide: Up to $200 per calendar year per caregiver. Covers course fees at AIC-approved training providers.
howToAccess: Register for approved courses through AIC's caregiver training portal. Claim reimbursement after course completion.

name: Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF)
description: Financial assistance for assistive devices (wheelchairs, walkers, hearing aids) and minor home modifications (grab bars, ramps) to help seniors age safely at home.
eligibility: Singapore Citizens and PRs aged 60 and above (or persons with disabilities). Means testing applies. Devices must be from approved suppliers.
costGuide: Subsidy of 50%–90% of cost depending on means testing. E.g., grab bar installation may cost $500 full; senior pays $50–$250 after subsidy.
howToAccess: Apply through an AIC-appointed Senior Care Centre, polyclinic, or hospital occupational therapist. AIC hotline: 1800-650-6060.

name: CareShield Life
description: Mandatory long-term care insurance for Singapore Citizens and PRs born in 1980 or later. Provides monthly cash payouts when the insured becomes severely disabled (unable to perform 3+ of 6 Activities of Daily Living).
eligibility: Mandatory for SC/PR born 1980 or later from age 30. Voluntary for those born 1979 or earlier if not on ElderShield.
costGuide: Monthly premium based on age and gender (approx. $200–$400/year at age 30). Payout from $600/month, increasing annually.
howToAccess: Auto-enrolled via CPF Board for those eligible. Check your policy at cpf.gov.sg or call CPF at 1800-227-1188.

name: MediFund
description: Government endowment fund that helps Singapore Citizens who cannot afford their medical bills after exhausting MediShield Life and Medisave. Applied at point of discharge or treatment.
eligibility: Singapore Citizens only. Must have exhausted MediShield Life and Medisave. Assessed by medical social worker at the institution.
costGuide: Covers outstanding bills after all other schemes. No fixed quantum — assessed case by case.
howToAccess: Speak to the Medical Social Worker at the hospital, polyclinic, or approved institution. No direct application needed.

name: Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) — Care Navigation
description: AIC is Singapore's central agency coordinating community care. Their care advisors help seniors and caregivers find the right services, initiate referrals, and navigate the care landscape.
eligibility: Open to all seniors and caregivers in Singapore. No means testing for navigation support.
howToAccess: Call AIC hotline at 1800-650-6060 (Mon–Fri 8:30am–8:30pm, Sat 8:30am–4pm). Walk in to any AIC touchpoint at public hospitals.

name: Community Case Management Service (CCMS)
description: Intensive, ongoing case management for seniors with complex needs — coordinating multiple services across health and social care, monitoring wellbeing, and managing care transitions.
eligibility: Seniors with complex or multiple care needs who require active coordination. Referral via hospital, polyclinic, or AIC.
costGuide: Subsidised service. Minimal or no charge for eligible seniors.
howToAccess: Referral through hospital Medical Social Worker, AIC, or polyclinic. Call AIC at 1800-650-6060.

name: Care Corner ICCP (Integrated Community Care Programme)
description: Care Corner provides integrated community care in selected sub-regions, coordinating health and social services for seniors with complex needs. Their coordinators provide personal, ongoing support and warm linkage to services.
eligibility: Seniors in Care Corner's designated service areas with complex care needs. Referral or self-referral accepted.
costGuide: Subsidised coordination service. Individual services may have separate fees.
howToAccess: Call Care Corner at 6353 1180 or email enquiries@carecorner.org.sg. AIC can also refer.

name: Hospital Medical Social Worker
description: Hospital-based social workers who assess discharge readiness, coordinate post-discharge community care, connect families with financial schemes, and provide counselling during care transitions.
eligibility: Patients admitted to restructured hospitals. Available to all patients; no separate eligibility criteria.
costGuide: Free service included in hospital admission.
howToAccess: Ask your ward nurse or doctor to refer you to the Medical Social Worker during hospitalisation. Critical to engage early, before discharge.
contactInfo: Contact your hospital's admissions / ward directly.
